spec.intent: Census @a67c4816 (design at a67c4816 plus documentation and persona, defined 2026-10-01T17:27Z); every path is repo-relative on the plan's line. A line number, count or observed behaviour cited here is a measurement at that commit: re-derive it if its path changed since. Rewrite the package READMEs a corpus author or library user reads (packages/forge/README.md 477 lines, packages/runtime/README.md 153, packages/schema/README.md 87, packages/canon/README.md 94, packages/tooling/README.md 24) from the finished tree, kept apart from the consumer's material. Each says what its package is for and how its own surface is used, and links out for the rest: what every package is for to ARCHITECTURE.md, anything a consumer does (install and its flags, practices, launching an agent by name, the badge, uninstall) to packages/cli/README.md, which another unit of this plan makes the one home of those facts. packages/forge/README.md today repeats consumer facts that packages/cli/README.md also holds (the install flags at :350-351, launch commands at :277-290, the badge at :299-320, install and uninstall at :345-425); keep only what an author of a corpus or of a harness adapter uses there (the pipeline, the port's fields, the deploy placement table, the library surface) and link for the rest. Its 'What used to be here' section is history; cut what the commits already hold. Settle the note 'two stale package README sentences': packages/canon/README.md:79-80 says canon takes defineAgentPlugin from @cratylus/forge at its plugin entry, which moved to @cratylus/schema; packages/tooling/README.md:5 says the package's scope is @repo, while it is named @cratylus/tooling and kept private by `private: true`. packages/canon/README.md describes the agents the plugin carries as persona-residue of this plan lands them: architect, planner, implementer, assayer and integrator are the generic holders of their roles, and mav, nico and kino are personas over the architect role. packages/runtime/README.md states the four built-in capabilities and the three domains as the runtime ships them. Every statement matches the code when the unit lands: check each claim against the package's src and run what a claim says runs. Keep packages/canon/test/command-veracity.test.ts green (every command a README tells a reader to run must exist). Persona wording: prose says persona only for an agent named as an individual (mav, nico, kino) and agent for any installed agent; a shipped identifier, flag, manifest key or path that spells persona for every agent (--link-persona-commands, --no-link-persona-commands, personaLinks, personas/ scope directories, cratylus-persona-badge, harness-persona-root, the Persona axis) is quoted verbatim as the code spells it, since renaming it waits on the ruling asked for in the note 'persona spelled for every agent in forge and schema'. A link into a file another unit of this plan writes (the ground documents, the package READMEs, docs/, packages/cli/README.md, README.md) names the file only, never a #fragment. Add a patch changeset for each published package whose README changes.

`git grep -n -E -- "--(no-)?link-persona-commands|--practices|--all\b" -- packages/forge/README.md packages/runtime/README.md packages/schema/README.md packages/canon/README.md packages/tooling/README.md` prints nothing

every line of the five READMEs that matches /persona/i also matches /\b(mav|nico|kino)\b|persona-commands|personaLinks|personas\/|persona-badge|Persona'|harness-persona-root|PersonaCommands|personaRootOf/
every relative link in the five READMEs resolves to a path tracked at the landing commit, and none that points into README.md, packages/cli/README.md, docs/ or a ground document carries a #fragment
